# DevLog-007 correctness fixtures

These small binary GDSII files isolate geometry semantics needed by the
web-only viewer. Their `*.semantic.json` companions are deterministic semantic
truth generated by reading the written GDS back with gdstk.

| Fixture | Contract under test |
| --- | --- |
| `non_default_dbu` | The file declares a 5 nm database unit; integer DBU coordinates must not be reinterpreted as 1 nm. |
| `transformed_sref` | Rotation, X reflection, magnification, and translation compose correctly for asymmetric geometry. |
| `skewed_aref` | Both components of the rotated AREF lattice vectors `(7, 3)` and `(-3, 7)` µm survive parsing and expansion. |
| `multiple_top_cells` | All document bounds include both top cells while the UI can require one active top-cell selection. |

The JSON stores coordinates in canonical integer DBU wherever possible and in
micrometers for inspection. `documentBounds*` is the union of every top cell;
`flattenedTopCells` keeps the per-top-cell geometry separate.

Regenerate in an isolated environment:

```sh
uv run --python 3.13 --with gdstk==1.0.1 python scripts/devlog-007/generate_fixtures.py
```

Or use a conventional virtual environment:

```sh
python3 -m venv /tmp/gdsjam-fixtures
/tmp/gdsjam-fixtures/bin/pip install -r scripts/devlog-007/requirements.txt
/tmp/gdsjam-fixtures/bin/python scripts/devlog-007/generate_fixtures.py
```

The generator fixes GDS timestamps and canonicalizes polygon rings, so running
it twice with the pinned gdstk version must leave all tracked outputs unchanged.
